headline: Decart's Lucy 2.5 enables real-time AI video editing with sub-40ms latency for live streams
summary: Decart AI's Lucy 2.5 model offers sub-40ms latency for live video editing, transforming streams instantly. It redefines the workflow for creators, from VTubing to live commerce.
details: Decart AI has released Lucy 2.5, an AI model that edits video frames in real time during a live stream. It achieves sub-40ms latency at 30 FPS, meaning AI transformations are pushed to the audience almost instantly after a gesture on camera.

This breakthrough shifts from "record first, edit later" to compressing video editing into the gap between frames. Traditional AI video tools require waiting for rendering, downloading, and importing, which is impractical for real-time audience interaction.

Lucy 2.5's innovation lies in "transformation" rather than "generation," rewriting an existing video stream in real time. Streamers see the edited version in OBS, which is exactly what their audience receives, thanks to Decart's proprietary DOS inference stack.

A key challenge in live AI video editing, temporal drift, is addressed by Lucy 2.5's Self-Anchoring feature. The model periodically uses its own output as a new reference frame, ensuring edits remain stable for minutes without degradation.

The model ships with 8 editing types, including background swaps, virtual try-ons, and character transformations, supporting combined text prompts and reference image control. This allows for precise adjustments like changing a background to a coffee shop or matching exact colors.

While costing $72/hour for live editing, the ROI is significant for conversion-heavy scenarios. Virtual try-on, for instance, can reduce return rates by 40% and boost conversion by 3x, making it cost-effective for short, impactful uses.

Lucy 2.5 is API-only, requiring no local GPU, with Decart handling inference. It integrates with OBS via WebRTC and offers Android and iOS SDKs, making it accessible for developers familiar with these technologies.
